newsitem.title: FRANCE: Court rejects challenge to Credit Foncier takeover.
newsitem.headline: Court rejects challenge to Credit Foncier takeover.

text.p: A Paris appeals court on Wednesday rejected a challenge by representatives of minority shareholders to a takeover offer for property lender Credit Foncier which is being made on the government's behalf by state bank Caisse de Depots et Consignations.
The appeals court rejected a challenge by a minority shareholders group called Adam, which sought to block the takeover offer of 70 francs a share.

Credit Foncier is being taken over as part of what finance minister Jean Arthuis has described as a "managed wind-down" that would cost about 2.6 billion francs if all shareholders accepted the CDC state bank offer which close on November 22.
Trading in Credit Foncier shares was suspended at 1300 GMT on Wednesday, when the stock stood at 69.15 francs, pending the court's verdict.

Arthuis announced plans to wind the group down last July on the grounds there was no other option after the group reported a 1995 loss of 10.8 billion francs and provisions of 13.6 billion francs for risky property loans and investments.

The minority shareholders group have resisted the move and sought more money while trade unions at Credit Foncier said the accounts had been overloaded with provisions and that it could actually survive.
The property lender bucked all expectations to report a net attributable profit of 402 million francs for the first half of 1996.
But the wind-down plan is now underway and the Caisse de Depots needs acceptances from two-thirds of shareholders for the takeover to proceed.
